name: Dorsoulnar approach to the 5th metacarpal base
aliases: dorsoulnar approach to the small finger CMC/base
corridor: Small dorsoulnar window over the fifth metacarpal base exposing the extensor carpi ulnaris insertion, protecting the dorsal sensory branch of the ulnar nerve

positioning.text: Position supine with the hand pronated on a hand table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Identify the extensor carpi ulnaris insertion on the ulnar base of the fifth metacarpal and the dorsal sensory branch of the ulnar nerve crossing the base.

incision.text: Make a small longitudinal incision over the dorsoulnar aspect of the metacarpal base.

superficial_interval.text: Protect the dorsal sensory branch of the ulnar nerve in the subcutaneous tissue and use blunt dissection to expose the extensor carpi ulnaris insertion.

deep_interval.text: Expose the metacarpal base subperiosteally at the extensor carpi ulnaris insertion for fixation or intramedullary wire entry.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with the dorsal ulnar sensory nerve, the extensor carpi ulnaris insertion, and the fifth metacarpal base.

structures_at_risk.text: The dorsal sensory branch of the ulnar nerve at the base and the extensor carpi ulnaris tendon are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The dorsoulnar base is the danger zone for the dorsal sensory branch of the ulnar nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Protect the dorsal ulnar sensory nerve and avoid detaching the extensor carpi ulnaris insertion unnecessarily.

exposure.text: Exposes the fifth metacarpal base and the extensor carpi ulnaris insertion.

limitations.text: The window is small and focused on the base, giving limited diaphyseal exposure.

indications.text: Indicated for fifth metacarpal base and avulsion fractures and as an entry for intramedullary wiring of neck fractures.

closure.text: Cover the implant with periosteum as far as possible, repair any cut intertendinous connection, and close the skin.

complications.text: Complications include dorsal ulnar sensory nerve injury and extensor carpi ulnaris irritation.

procedure_applications.condition: A fifth metacarpal base or avulsion fracture, or a neck fracture treated with intramedullary wiring, needs a basal entry

questions.question: Which tendon inserts on the ulnar base of the fifth metacarpal?
What is this approach used for besides base fractures?
questions.answer: As an entry for intramedullary wire fixation of extraarticular neck fractures.

questions.question: Which nerve is at greatest risk at the base?
questions.answer: The dorsal sensory branch of the ulnar nerve.
